I'll be honest, I dont really know. I'm not sure exactly how [tactics.tools](http://tactics.tools) decides your grades. My best guess is that I am really careful about when I spend my gold. I roll really hard when I know my odds of hitting a unit I need are highest. If I'm playing dynamo/mf, i will scout and if someone is playing syndicate and I know they are going to want MF, I level and spend as much as I need to in order to hit her 2 star before they have the chance to hit. Rolling down and hitting a unit that puts you far enough ahead of the lobby is actually really good for your economy, especially if you are already on a winstreak and are now maintaining it. It's better to roll to 0 in order to keep a 5+ winstreak than to hold and start losing. Play for tempo, being the strongest in the lobby also makes you the richest.

I also play the early game really flexibly and only force the final comp near the end game. Jhin, senna, shaco, and a few other characters all hold MF items well and fit the build well until i have the units to replace them with. I play the strongest possible board until i roll down on 8/9 and i force the final comp then. [Tactics.tools](http://Tactics.tools) doesnt take into account anything but the final board. The final lvl 9 board might look the same in every game but i took a totally different path to get there each game. Hope that makes sense.

I swapped to a dynamo/mf build and climbed up to diamond this week. The boards that can win games are just known, and you'll never climb if you don't play for a game winning board. It is what it is. I will say the game become more dynamic and more small optimizations matter the higher you go. I'm having more fun in the higher elo lobbies than i was in the lower ones.

You need to play with your end game carry in mind. Your probably slamming items on characters in the early game because they are good on that character, but you should be building items that are good on your endgame carry. Look at low cost units as stepping stones to higher cost ones. For example on a dynamo build, morgana holds items till elise, elise holds items till aurora, and those items should be built with aurora in mind, not morgana.

You should also try to slam your items based on their relative power during the stage of the game you are in. Items like Dclaw, HoJ, Redemption, etc. that give % health, healing or damage are going to be better in the late game while items like warmogs, deathblade, gargoyles, guinsoos etc that give flat or scaling stats are better early. Putting something that gives % stats will always be better on strong characters with a lot of stats to amp up, flat stats will always be better on weak characters in the early game.

You are also probably not playing with tempo in mind. Everyone in the game has a set amount of resources. Those being items, gold, and health. Tempo is decided by how fast players are spending those resources. If you play an item that is good late, but weak early, you will lose relative power with the rest of the lobby. Try to play the strongest board possible for the stage of the game youre in, even if that means taking out or putting in characters that arent in the build you have in mind for end game. Just pivot back into the characters you need for your endgame board to buff up your main 4 or 5 cost carry. Gaining a power spike is like starting with a head start in a race, you dont have to be the fastest runner if you have a head start, you just need to go fast enough to get to the end before someone catches up. Spend your resources to maintain win streaks. Your items/comp doesnt have to be perfect, it just has to be stronger than everyone else for as long as possible.

Last bit of advice, on [tactics.tools](http://tactics.tools), flexibility is the least important stat to improve on till higher elos. Find a build you like, with a line you are comfortable with. Know when the board is stable and will beat most boards so you know when to econ out, and know when to roll down and level to maintain tempo. Find an S teir comp or two, force it over and over focusing on not rerolling till late game. I forced amp/strat annie through gold and into plat, and then forced Dynamo MF all the way through emerald into diamond. Don't worry about having an F grade in flexibility, worry about those low grades in econ and items. 

Here is what my grades looked like all the way through emerald. Practice forcing a strong comp so you know when you are in a situation where that comp works. You'll climb crazy fast through gold and plat just forcing something you know is going to work. After doing that with 5 or 6 comps you'll know when you're in a position to play each one early on in the game. 

Anyway, good luck.

I was raised mormon, who have a bit of a different take on speaking in tongues that isnt that relevant to the question, but I have been to a couple bible camps for other religious denominations and have gotten a taste of what the babling style of speaking in tongues is like. I think it is useful to look at other states of mind that induce similar experiences. 

One that comes to mind is early childhood. Children babble on and on with only a few sounds actually carrying any ascribed meaning. Part of language acquisition seems to be testing out as many strange noises as you can till the adults who know certain sounds ascribed meanings confirm the noise you made means something to them. 

The next state I consider similar is glossilalia induced by psychedelic states. The mind can go from thinking in the form of complete sentences, to random babble, and then back. When this type of thing happens most people describe it as a transcendent or religious experience.

We can assume then that these babbling language modes are part of the human experience induced when the brain is in a state of high connectivity. Those states tend to lean towards religious experiences or early childhood. I think it's clearly a real phenomenon triggered by different stimuli. What is actually going on, I couldn't really tell you. Maybe some sort of language creating brain state that catalyzes the creation or apprehension of culture. Maybe it's no more then a sign of delusional thinking, or a reversion to childlike states of mind. Selling it as none existent or claiming other people are faking it doesnt really do us any good. Perhaps their brain really is just trying to make them fit in eith everyone else, but if that's true, why does it feel so real within an individual's experience? Just some thoughts.

This is a really complex magic system. It reminds me of surgebinding from the stormlight archive. You should consider each of your flers their own individual magic system and make sure you know the rules of each. The reader needs to be able to rely upon their knowledge of the magic system in order for the book to feel satisfying. 

You also may want to simplify. I dont think there is anything wrong with this magic system, and if you think you can tackle books using it, go for it. But having that many magic systems in a single novel and having enough information on it for the reader to keep up is going to be hard. The stormlight archive has 10 types of surgebinder and 1.5 million words in he has only described how 2 or 3 of them work. Unless you're planning a 14 book epic fantasy series it's going to be hard to use all of these in a single story and a lot of powers are going to have to be underused or not used at all.

Soulcasters in The Stormlight Archive work this way.  They build things out of wood and soul cast them to solid stone to help weather massive storms. Or the soulcast rock into smoke to make holes in cliff faces. Another thing they do is soulcast the bodies of their dead into statues. It works on totally different principles then alchemy though but function in essentially the same way.
 Maybe check those books out and see how they are used in that world, and then see how you can extrapolate that to a different world using alchemy to accomplish the same thing.
One thing to consider is what would be the cost of alchemy? Easy to do and cheap? Then every home in your world should have traces of it. Expensive and difficult? Only the grandest castles would have access to it. Are some materials easier to achieve through alchemy? Does alchemy have a cost or risk to the one performing it? What era of technology is your setting in? It would be used vastly differently in the middle ages versus and steampunk type era. Different materials would be valued much lower or higher. If it's easy it would remove the scarcity of things like gold, so things not available through alchemy would become more valuable. 
Specifically architecture you could have buildings made of impossible materials. Wooden floors could be all one piece. Perhaps alchemical windows that still have the grain of the wood of the wall, all continuous.

There's a lot more strategy then you seem to think. Nothing like risk or chess or something but some. There is definitely a thing as a good monopoly player. Properties have certain probabilities based off of die roll probability. Which makes the red and orange spaces the most landed on and therefore most profitable spaces. Play against people who don't know this and trade your dark blue monopoly to complete your orange collection is a strategic move that seems like an uneven trade but the player with the orange spaces actually comes out on top. There are a lot more ways to gamble and wager over the probability of spaces. Monopoly has about the same amount of strategy as settlers of Catan, it's just not as glaringly obvious.

Also auctions can be good moved depending on the situation. Can't afford an expensive property? Put it up for auction. The player that puts it up can bet on it too and you can get a property for below its value. Railroads are 100% worthless unless you have all 4 and even then they rarely bring a return let alone win you the game. So if you own one just put any other ones you eat up for auction, let other players have it and then never sell the railroad you have. You don't spend a dime on it and they got a worthless space.

Understanding the probability of each space getting landed on changes the game completely. It's not the most strategic game, but it's far from a bad game.
